items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Mosley Interview, 1961-09-23
items.q: That's where my name was playing on that old cabaretts down there on Rampart Street. That was the blue light district all down there during that time. Katie White and all that.

ctx.x: And over there, they talk a lot about like downtown sometimes and uptown. Some of the downtown people never did get across Canal Street. They say, well, they're like... Well, you got people right down there now.

I know some family that have never seen the river. Really? On and raised here. That's right. Haven't seen the river. And they haven't been nowhere. The only one thing they've been downtown. They were ripe age, you know, and some of them died. And I seen people down there, live down there. Old people told me they never seen the Congo Parade. Live farther down, you know. Yeah. Like around the Ninth Ward all down there. Yeah. Well, it was just during that time, it was just like a country down there on the other side…
That'd be in the dance hall.
